assay_targets_or_enrichments.ontology_label: Chemical cross-linking coupled with mass spectrometry proteomics

acquisition: MS1 spectra were acquired with a resolution of 120,000 in the orbitrap (OT)
Dynamic exclusion was set to 30 seconds
MS2 spectra were recorded with a resolution of 30,000 in OT and the isolation window set to 1.6 m/z
labeling: No labeling reagents mentioned; standard tryptic digestion and LC-MS/MS
enrichment: Cross-linked peptides were resuspended in 50 µl 30 % acetonitrile/0.1 % TFA and enriched by peptide size exclusion chromatography/pSEC (Superdex Peptide PC3.2/300 column, GE Healthcare, flow rate 50 µl/min)
incubated with 1″mM of bissulfosuccinimidyl suberate (BS3) for 45″minutes at 4°C
workflow_hints: Chemical cross-linking coupled with mass spectrometry proteomics
Cross-links were displayed with xiNET and XlinkAnalyzer

Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a classic XL-MS (Cross-linking Mass Spectrometry) study using BS3 as the cross-linker. Acquisition is DDA based on the use of dynamic exclusion and precursor isolation windows. The 'mod_complexome' modifier is selected as the most appropriate routing for structural/complex-based cross-linking analysis.

scope: To prepare a sample for performing cross-linking mass-spectrometry, a stable complex of SNAPc-containing Pol-II PIC bound to U5 promoter was isolated.

An assay containing Pol II, TBP, TFIIA, TFIIB, TFIIF and SNAPc-FL was incubated in ratios explained above and was subjected to size-exclusion chromatography using Superose 6 increase 3.2/300 GL column (GE Healthcare)
The peak fractions were then pooled and incubated with 1 mM of bissulfosuccinimidyl suberate (BS3) for 45 minutes at 4 °C.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The material analyzed by LC-MS/MS was a reconstituted and purified pre-initiation complex (PIC) isolated via size-exclusion chromatography, not a whole cell lysate.

evidence: To prepare a sample for performing cross-linking mass-spectrometry, a stable complex of SNAPc-containing Pol-II PIC bound to U5 promoter was isolated.
Peptides were loaded in duplicates onto a Dionex Ultimate 3000 RSLCnano

biological_variables: To prepare a sample for performing cross-linking mass-spectrometry, a stable complex of SNAPc-containing Pol-II PIC bound to U5 promoter was isolated.
design: Peptides were loaded in duplicates onto a Dionex Ultimate 3000 RSLCnano

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry component of this study is a structural characterization using chemical cross-linking (XL-MS) to map interactions within a reconstituted protein complex (SNAPc-containing Pol II PIC). There is no differential biological perturbation, treatment, or case-control comparison performed via MS; it is a descriptive structural analysis of a single complex state. Therefore, it is mapped as un-classified.

base_candidates_ranked.reason: Data was acquired using DDA (Orbitrap Exploris) and analyzed for cross-links, but no specific labeling (SILAC/Isobaric) is mentioned.

modifier_candidates_ranked.reason: Explicit use of BS3 cross-linker and analysis via pLink 2.3.9 for cross-linked peptide-spectrum matches.

workflow: The peak fractions were then pooled and incubated with 1 mM of bissulfosuccinimidyl suberate (BS3) for 45 minutes
Cross-linked peptides derived from pSEC were subjected to liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC–MS) on a Thermo Orbitrap Exploris mass spectrometer
analyzed via pLink 2.3.9 at a false discovery rate (FDR) of 1%
Cross-links were displayed with xiNET and XlinkAnalyzer
differential: For further analysis, only interaction sites with three cross-linked peptide-spectrum matches were taken into account.
search_parameters: Carbamidomethylation of cysteines was set as fixed modification and oxidation of methionines as variable modification.

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: This is a CXMS (Cross-linking Mass Spectrometry) experiment using the BS3 reagent. The primary goal was to identify interaction sites to validate structural models, not to perform quantitative differential abundance analysis.
